clue.text: Not far from West End, see a club, perhaps

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near, not far from

indicators.note: the end of West is its last letter, picked out on its own

parts.note: to spot something is to see it

explanation.surface: Directions to a club a short way from London's West End theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatre district, but 'End' only picks the last letter of West, T. 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightspot is a nightclub, so a club is an example of one, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Pass from head I had

parts.note: nob is slang for the head
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A ball passed from the head of a player who once had it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' is the bridge call made when not bidding.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, saying 'no bid' is how a player passes.

clue.text: Rotating piece of machinery breaking leg, we hear

indicators.note: breaking the words up lets their letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A gear tooth breaking someone's leg, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' looks like a sound-alike signal, but its letters are fodder with LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A gearwheel is a toothed wheel that turns to transmit drive in a machine.

clue.text: Tango, on radio, composer conducted was moving

parts.note: Tango is the radio code word for the letter T
Ravel was a French composer
to conduct is to lead, so led

explanation.surface: A tango broadcast on the radio, its composer conducting it on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on radio' says Tango is the radio alphabet's word for T, not a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelled means went from place to place, was moving.

clue.text: Fieldworker's midday fare never free?

parts.note: a pub meal named after a farm labourer, with a nod to the saying that there is no such thing as a free lunch

explanation.surface: A farmhand's lunch always has to be paid for.
explanation.walkthrough: A ploughman's lunch is a British pub dish of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: The pub dish is literally the noon meal of one who ploughs, a fieldworker.

clue.text: As one taking highly risky steps, I get help with artwork, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone in a precarious position asking for help with their art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the fodder and gives no letters. 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightrope walker steps along a high wire, each step a risk.

clue.text: Kind of pub that doesn't put anyone out?

definitions.meaning: a regular's neighbourhood pub, the one nearest home
describing an anaesthetic that numbs one part of the body without making the patient unconscious

explanation.definitionFit: A local is a nearby pub; a local anaesthetic numbs a spot without knocking the patient out.

clue.text: Weapon corporal may have at the front

definitions.meaning: a long spear carried by a mounted soldier

definitions.text: corporal may have at the front
definitions.meaning: a ... corporal is the lowest rank of non-commissioned officer

explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a cavalry spear; a lance corporal's rank has this word at its front.

clue.text: One of the reptiles on island — they come out in spring

parts.note: a croc is a crocodile

explanation.surface: A crocodile on an island, and creatures that emerge in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Croci, plural of crocus, are flowers that bloom in early spring.

clue.text: Having been wronged, I got trial?

definitions.text: Having been wronged, I got trial?

indicators.note: the words are treated wrongly, put out of their right order

explanation.surface: Someone who has suffered a wrong ends up going to court.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigator takes a grievance to court, so the wronged party seeking a trial is one.

clue.text: Boasting, for female performer, excellent serve

parts.note: brava is the cry of praise for a woman performer, the feminine form of bravo
to do can mean to serve or suffice, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: A tennis commentator gushing over a woman player's superb serve.
explanation.walkthrough: Opera audiences shout BRAVO to a man and BRAVA to a woman; 'serve' is not tennis but DO, as in 'that will do'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a swaggering show of daring, close in sense to boastful display.

clue.text: Armed vessel multinational group and British used in attack

indicators.note: used in says these two pieces are put inside the word meaning attack

parts.note: to go at someone is to attack them
UN is the United Nations, a multinational body

explanation.surface: A warship from a UN coalition and Britain deployed in an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attack' is two words, go at, run together as one; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunboat is a small warship carrying guns, an armed vessel.

clue.text: Search for water to put fire out

definitions.meaning: dowsing is hunting for underground water with a divining rod
to douse, also spelt this way, is to extinguish a flame

explanation.definitionFit: Dowsing is divining for water; the same spelling is a variant of douse, meaning to extinguish.

clue.text: Grand operas collectively gripping a crowd

indicators.note: gripping says the grand-plus-operas piece holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds
The Ring is Wagner's cycle of four operas taken together

explanation.surface: Grand operas performed as a set that hold a big audience spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's four operas, Der Ring des Nibelungen, are known together as THE RING; G and THE RING together hold A just after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering is an assembly of people, a crowd come together.

clue.text: Live and prosper, none the less

indicators.note: read literally, minus a nought: the letter like zero is taken away

parts.note: to do well is to prosper

explanation.surface: A version of the Vulcan blessing 'live long and prosper', regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'none the less' looks like 'nevertheless' but means 'with the O (nought) removed' from DO WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live there, reside.

clue.text: Exploit, in one kind of belief, a hopeless attitude

indicators.note: in says the deed goes inside the word for the belief

parts.note: deism is belief in a creator who does not intervene
a feat is a notable exploit or deed

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of a hopeless outlook within some faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' looks like a verb but is the noun, a feat.
explanation.definitionFit: Defeatism is the expectation of failure, an attitude without hope.

clue.text: Do extra work to get satellite to land

parts.note: the Moon is Earth's natural satellite
to light on something is to land or settle on it, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Advice that taking on a second job will get a spacecraft onto the Moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' is the verb light, as in alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To moonlight is to take a second job on the side, doing extra work.

clue.text: Brightness of man, in clue originally seen

indicators.note: originally here means arranged in an original, novel way

explanation.surface: Seeing a man's brilliance first shown in a crossword clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like a first-letters signal but asks for an original rearrangement. 'of' and 'seen' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Luminance is a measure of brightness, the light given off by a surface.

clue.text: Award nobody runs up to get

definitions.text: Award nobody runs up to get

parts.words: Award nobody runs up to get
parts.note: the prize for coming first, which a runner-up, the one finishing second, never receives

explanation.surface: A prize that nobody makes an effort to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs up' reads as making an effort; split it as runner-up.
explanation.definitionFit: First place in Olympic events earns this top award, never given to the runner-up.

clue.text: Excitedly flocked around an ethnic performance

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround the next word
an excited arrangement of the letters scrambles them

explanation.surface: A crowd rushed eagerly to surround a traditional cultural show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excitedly' scrambles the bird-flock verb into FOLKDCE, which then wraps 'around' the little word just after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A folk dance is a traditional dance of a people, a performance of their culture.

clue.text: Half-hearted storyteller is one who competes in the long run

definitions.text: one who competes in the long run

indicators.note: half of the doubled letter in the middle is lost, so the heart is halved

parts.note: the Miller is one of the tellers of tales in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales

explanation.surface: A storyteller lacking enthusiasm is the one who keeps going over time.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaucer's Miller tells a tale; 'Half-hearted' removes one of the two central Ls. 'the long run' is a mile race, not 'eventually'.
explanation.definitionFit: A miler is an athlete who runs the mile, a long race by sprint standards.

clue.text: Commonwealth has small area left in part of Europe

indicators.note: in says these letters are placed within the European country

parts.note: Austria is a country in central Europe
A is the abbreviation, the short form, for area

explanation.surface: A country of the Commonwealth with little land left in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small area' is the abbreviated area, A, and L for left; both go inside AUSTRIA after AUSTR.
explanation.definitionFit: The country's formal name is the Commonwealth of Australia.

clue.text: It can help to achieve one's aim, in a sense

definitions.text: It can help to achieve one's aim
definitions.meaning: the device on a gun that a marksman looks along to aim
vision, one of the five senses

explanation.definitionFit: A gun's sight assists aiming; sight is also the faculty of vision, one of the senses.

clue.text: Cash presented as bills — yen

parts.note: bills in Parliament are read, a first reading presents them to the House
Y is the abbreviation for yen, the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: Money offered in banknotes, in Japanese yen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bills' are not banknotes but parliamentary bills, which are read. 'the ready' is slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready, as in ready money or the readies, is informal for cash.

clue.text: He's wandering but sane, according to Scots

indicators.note: in Scots speech 'no' stands for not, so the T of the English word is dropped

parts.note: a sane person is not mad, two words run together

explanation.surface: A Scot vouching that a drifter is perfectly sane.
explanation.walkthrough: Scots say 'no' for not, hence 'according to Scots' trims the T. 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad roams from place to place without a settled home, a wanderer.

clue.text: Model that all the players can see after play starts

definitions.text: that all the players can see after play starts
definitions.meaning: in bridge, the hand laid face up on the table after the opening lead

explanation.definitionFit: A dummy is a mannequin or model; in bridge the dummy hand is exposed once play begins.

clue.text: Wet outside, having switched pieces to dye thus

indicators.note: the two parts of the word swap places, the front going to the back

parts.note: when it is raining it is wet out of doors

explanation.surface: Bad weather outside, with fabric dyed in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: RAINING split as RAIN and ING, then swapped. Fabric dyed in the grain, that is the fibre before weaving, was said to be ingrained.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingrain originally meant to dye fibre in the grain, before it was woven into cloth.

clue.text: Partly backing Dominican Republic? Not so!

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that the Dominican Republic is not really a republic at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is ruled by a monarch, the opposite of a republic.

clue.text: Decisive moment in game before end of rugby friendly

indicators.note: before places the chess word ahead of the next piece

parts.note: mate, checkmate, is the winning moment in chess

indicators.note: the end of rugby is its last letter

explanation.surface: A rugby friendly settled by a decisive moment just before the final whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'game' is chess, not the rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: Matey is a colloquial word for friendly and sociable.

clue.text: In rough sport, try to land on gym equipment

indicators.note: on places the angling word after the gym piece

parts.note: a vaulting horse is a piece of gymnastics apparatus
an angler plays a fish, tiring it out while trying to land it

explanation.surface: In a rough sport, an attempt to land on a vaulting horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try to land' is fishing: to play a hooked fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Horseplay is rough, boisterous play, rowdy fun.
